title: Jemperli with paclitaxel and carboplatin
context_label: dMMR/MSI-H advanced or recurrent endometrial cancer
schedule_label: Three medicines every 3 weeks for six planned cycles. The first Jemperli-only visit is 3 weeks after cycle six. After that, Jemperli is given every 6 weeks.
schedule_summary: Three medicines every 3 weeks for six planned cycles. The first Jemperli-only visit is 3 weeks after cycle six. After that, Jemperli is given every 6 weeks.
purpose: The aim is to control womb cancer that is advanced or has returned, and delay it getting worse.
indication_text: This Irish regimen requires a tumour test showing mismatch repair deficiency (dMMR) or high microsatellite instability (MSI-H). Your team explains what the result means for you.
administration_text: On combination days, dostarlimab goes into a vein first, then paclitaxel, then carboplatin. The paclitaxel infusion usually takes about three hours. Allow extra time for checks, premedicines and observation.
monitoring_summary: Immune inflammation can start between visits or after treatment ends. Keep the immunotherapy alert card and show it to every team caring for you.
review_status: Feasibility build; independent oncology, pharmacy and patient review pending

agents.name: Dostarlimab
agents.explanation: It removes a brake on immune cells so they can recognise and attack cancer. It can also cause inflammation in healthy organs.
agents.mechanism: It removes a brake on immune cells so they can recognise and attack cancer. It can also cause inflammation in healthy organs.
agents.watch: Report new cough, diarrhoea, severe fatigue or rash even after the final dose.
visual: It removes a brake on immune cells so they can recognise and attack cancer. It can also cause inflammation in healthy organs.

agents.name: Paclitaxel
agents.explanation: It disrupts cell division. Hair follicles, blood cells and nerves can also be affected.
agents.mechanism: It disrupts cell division. Hair follicles, blood cells and nerves can also be affected.
agents.watch: Report numbness and tell the nurse immediately if you flush or wheeze during treatment.
visual: It disrupts cell division. Hair follicles, blood cells and nerves can also be affected.

agents.name: Carboplatin
agents.explanation: It damages DNA in dividing cells. Kidney function helps determine the prescribed amount.
agents.mechanism: It damages DNA in dividing cells. Kidney function helps determine the prescribed amount.
agents.watch: Report fever, bleeding, hearing changes or an infusion reaction.
visual: It damages DNA in dividing cells. Kidney function helps determine the prescribed amount.

common_effects.title: Nausea and fatigue
common_effects.text: Use the anti-sickness plan supplied for each phase. Call if vomiting prevents drinking.

common_effects.title: Hair and nerves
common_effects.text: Paclitaxel can cause hair loss and numbness. Report nerve changes before each infusion.

serious_effects.title: Dostarlimab and immune inflammation
serious_effects.text: Lung, bowel, liver, kidney, skin and hormone problems can begin after treatment stops. Call urgently for new breathlessness, diarrhoea, jaundice or marked weakness.

serious_effects.title: Paclitaxel and carboplatin
serious_effects.text: Fever, chills, bleeding or sudden illness need an immediate call. Report flushing, dizziness or wheeze during any infusion immediately.

phases.label: Cycles 1–6
phases.detail: Three infusions every three weeks if your team confirms you are ready.

phases.label: Cycle 7 onwards
phases.detail: Jemperli alone, then every six weeks. Your team reviews benefit and side effects. NCCP allows up to three years of monotherapy.

anatomy: Call urgently for new cough or breathlessness.
Report severe tiredness, headache, unusual thirst or dizziness.
New weakness needs urgent advice. Severe chest pain or collapse needs 112 or 999.
Call urgently for new diarrhoea, pain or blood in stools.
Call for yellow eyes or dark urine. Blood tests can also detect inflammation.
Hair loss is common with paclitaxel. A spreading, blistering or peeling rash needs urgent help.
Report tingling or numbness early, especially if walking or fastening buttons becomes difficult.
Call immediately for fever, shaking chills, sudden illness or unusual bleeding.
anatomy_note: Call for new or worsening symptoms.

questions.q: Which medicines stop after cycle six, when is the first maintenance visit, and which symptoms would make you call today?
questions.a: Review your personal plan with the team before leaving.

questions.q: Who do I call outside clinic hours?
questions.a: Ask the team to complete both numbers on the wallet card and agree a backup contact.

support.title: Combination phase
support.text: Carboplatin carries high sickness risk. Follow the scheduled anti-sickness medicines and the rescue plan given by your team.

support.title: Paclitaxel premedicines
support.text: Before paclitaxel the unit provides medicines to reduce allergic reactions. Confirm any doses you must take at home before attending.

support.title: Jemperli alone
support.text: Sickness risk is minimal with Jemperli alone. Ask which medicines continue once chemotherapy ends. Keep carrying your immunotherapy alert card.

teachback: Which medicines stop after cycle six, when is the first maintenance visit, and which symptoms would make you call today?
consent_support: Discuss the expected benefit, side effects, fertility, alternatives and symptom-directed care with the treating clinician. You may ask for more time or change your decision.
safety_note: Fever, new breathlessness, diarrhoea or unusual bleeding? Call oncology now.
urgent_extra: Fever, new breathlessness, diarrhoea or unusual bleeding? Call oncology now.

evidence.title: Evidence behind this treatment
evidence.interpretation: In RUBY, adding dostarlimab to chemotherapy and then continuing dostarlimab reduced the hazard of progression or death in the dMMR/MSI-H group (HR 0.28, 95% CI 0.16–0.50).
evidence.limitations: These results compare groups over time. They cannot predict the duration of benefit for one person. The NCCP indication shown here is biomarker-specific.
